verses.zh: 以下是神人摩西在未死之先为以色列人所祝的福：
verses.en: This is the blessing Moses the man of God pronounced upon the Israelites before his death.
verses.commentary:
33:1 "the blessing. . .blessed" The VERB (BDB 138, KB 159, Piel PERFECT) and
the NOUN occur in Deut. 33:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING

▣ "the man of God" This phrase (BDB 35 CONSTRUCT BDB 43) was used to describe
prophets (cf. Josh. 14:6; 1 Sam. 2:27; 9:6-7; 1 Kgs. 9:6; 12:22; 13:1,30; 2 Kgs. 1:9-13; 5:8; 23:17; Jer. 35:4). Moses was a
prophet (i.e. Deut. 18:15).

verses.zh: 他说：耶和华从西奈而来，从西珥向他们显现，从巴兰山发出光辉，从万万圣者中来临，从他右手为百姓传出烈火的律法。
verses.en: He said:“The Lord came from Sinaiand revealed himself[NOTE:1] to Israel[NOTE:2] from Seir.He appeared in splendor[NOTE:3] from Mount Paran,and came forth with ten thousand holy ones.[NOTE:4] With his right hand he gave a fiery law[NOTE:5] to them.
notes: Or “rose like the sun” (NCV, TEV).

Heb “him”; the referent (Israel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.tc Heb “to him.” The LXX reads “to us” (לָנוּ [lanu] for לָמוֹ [lamo]), the reading of the MT is acceptable since it no doubt has in mind Israel as a collective singular.
Or “he shone forth” (NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

With slight alteration (מִמְרִבַת קָדֵשׁ [mimrivat qadesh] for the MT’s מֵרִבְבֹת קֹדֶשׁ [merivevot qodesh]) the translation would be “from Meribah Kadesh” (cf. NAB, NLT; see Deut 32:51). However, the language of holy war in the immediate context favors the reading of the MT, which views the Lord as accompanied by angelic hosts.
The mispointed Hebrew term אֵשְׁדָּת (ʾeshdat) should perhaps be construed as אֵשְׁהַת (ʾeshhat) with Smr.
verses.commentary:
33:2 This describes a revelatory appearance of YHWH to Israel (i.e. theophany). This awesome encounter between
the Divine and humans was terrifying (cf. Exodus 19; Ps. 50:2-3). YHWH's presence was continued in the form of the special
cloud (i.e, Shekinah cloud of glory; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH). YHWH
came and stayed with His people from Mt. Sinai/Horeb until they crossed the Jordan. Even then, His special presence was with the Ark,
above the wings of the cherubim.

It is obvious from this verse that YHWH is associated with mountains (cf. 1 Kgs. 20:23,28).

- Moriah (Gen. 22:2; 2 Chr. 3:1, site of the temple)

- Mt. Sinai/Horeb (Exodus 19-20)

- Mt. Seir (here, Jdg. 5:4)

- Mt. Paran (here, Hab. 3:3)

- Ebal/Gerizim (27:4; Josh. 8:30-33)

- Tabor (Jdgs. 4:6)

- Carmel (1 Kgs. 18:20-39; 2 Kgs. 4:25-27)

- Perazim (2 Sam. 5:20; Isa. 28:21)

- Mt. Zion (Isa. 2:1-4; Mic. 4:1-4; Ps. 68:16, name for Jerusalem)

- Mt. Nebo (Deuteronomy 34, to Moses only)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "Sinai" This is the place of the giving of the Law. It is called Sinai (BDB 696) only here in Deuteronomy. It is
usually called Horeb (BDB 352).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

▣ "Seir" This name (BDB 973) has several different referents in the OT:

- It can refer to the land of Edom ‒ Gen. 32:3; 36:30; Num. 24:18; Deut. 1:44; 2:8,12,22,29; 33:1; Josh. 11:17; Jdgs. 5:4.

- It can refer to a mountain/hill in Edom ‒ Gen. 36:8-9; Deut. 1:2; 2:14; Josh. 24:4.

- It can refer to a people ‒ Gen. 36:20-30; 2 Chr. 25:11,14; Ezek. 25:8 (of Edom)

- It can refer to a mountain/hill in Judah ‒ Josh. 15:10(?).

▣ "Mount Paran" This is the mountain range (BDB 803) close to the plains of Moab (cf. Deut. 1:1) on
the west side of Arabah, down the west side of the Gulf of Aqaba.

Perhaps this listing is of the travel of the children of Israel as they left Sinai going into the Promised
Land (also can be a wilderness, cf. Num. 10:12; 12:16; 13:3,26). God was saying that He had been with them throughout
the wanderings and He was still with them.

▣

NASB
"the midst of ten thousand holy ones"

NKJV, Peshitta
"with ten thousands of saints"

NRSV, REB
"myriads of holy ones"

TEV
"ten thousand angels were with him"

NJB
——

LXX
"with myriads of Kades"

The MT here has "Ribeboth-Kodesh." Deuteronomy 32:51 translates similar consonants as
"Meribah-Kadesh. This could refer to

- an unknown place name (JPSOA)

- "angels" (cf. Ps. 68:17; Dan. 7:10; Rev. 5:11)

- "saints" (LXX, cf. Deut. 7:6; 33:3; 14:2; 26:19; 28:9)

Rabbinical Midrash uses this as text to assert the intermediary role of angels (cf. Acts 7:53; Gal. 3:19; Heb. 2:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: holy ones

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

▣

NASB, JPSOA
"flashing lightning"

NKJV
"a fiery law"

NRSV
"a host of his own"

TEV
"a flaming fire"

NJB
"blazed forth"

NASB margin
"a fiery Law"

LXX
"angels with him"

Literally this is "fiery law" (BDB 77 and 206). However, in this context it refers to the coming glory of
the brilliance of YHWH's glory (cf. Isa. 60:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT, kabod)

verses.zh: 他疼爱百姓；众圣徒都在他手中。他们坐在他的脚下，领受他的言语。
verses.en: Surely he loves the people;[NOTE:1] all your holy ones[NOTE:2] are in your power.[NOTE:3] And they sit[NOTE:4] at your feet,each receiving[NOTE:5] your words.
notes: Heb “peoples.” The apparent plural form is probably a misunderstood singular (perhaps with a pronominal suffix) with enclitic mem (ם). See HALOT 838 s.v. עַם B.2.

Heb “his holy ones.” The third person masculine singular suffix of the Hebrew MT is problematic in light of the second person masculine singular suffix on בְּיָדֶךָ (beyadekha, “your hands”). The LXX versions by Lucian and Origen read, therefore, “the holy ones.” The LXX version by Theodotion and the Vulgate, however, presuppose third masculine singular suffix on בְּיָדָיו (beyadayv, “his hands”), and thus retain “his holy ones.” The efforts to bring pronominal harmony into the line is commendable but unnecessary given the Hebrew tendency to be untroubled by such grammatical inconsistencies. However, the translation harmonizes the first pronoun with the second so that the referent (the Lord) is clear.
Heb “hands.” For the problem of the pronoun see note on the term “holy ones” earlier in this verse.

The Hebrew term תֻּכּוּ (tukku, probably Pual perfect of תָּכָה, takhah) is otherwise unknown. The present translation is based on the reference to feet and, apparently, receiving instruction in God’s words (cf. KJV, ASV). Other options are as follows: NIV “At your feet they all bow down” (cf. NCV, CEV); NLT “They follow in your steps” (cf. NAB, NASB); NRSV “they marched at your heels.”
The singular verbal form in the Hebrew text (lit. “he lifts up”) is understood in a distributive manner, focusing on the action of each individual within the group.
verses.commentary:
33:3 "He loves the people" The VERB (BDB 285, KB 284, Qal PARTICIPLE) seems
to reflect Deut. 4:37; 7:7-8; 10:15.

The OBJECT "people" is PLURAL and refers to the descendants of the Patriarchs.

▣

NASB
"All Your holy ones are in Your hand"

NKJV
"All His saints are in your hand"

NRSV
"All his holy ones were in your charge"

TEV
"protects those who belong to him"

NJB
"Your holy ones are all at your command"

JPSOA footnote
"All His worshippers in your care"

REB
"blesses his holy ones"

LXX
"All of the sanctified ones under your hands"

The term "holy ones" (BDB 481 CONSTRUCT BDB 872) refers to the covenant
people. This could be translated "saints" (e.g. Deut. 7:6; 14:2,21; 26:19; 28:9; "holy people").

The JPSOA footnote says "the meaning of vv. 3-5 is uncertain." The Jewish Study Bible, p. 446, suggests
that "'the hallowed'" originally referred to the divine council but that the poem's editors shifted the focus to Israel." It
asserts that this was done to make sense of v. 4.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Holy Ones

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

▣

NASB, JPSOA, Peshitta
"followed"

NKJV
"sit down"

NRSV
"marched"

TEV
"bow"

NJB
"fell"

REB
"sit"

This is literally "lie down at" (BDB 1067, KB 1730, Pual PERFECT, unusual VERB
only here). It could also refer to the position of a learner

- bowed low, cf. TEV

- sit at your feet , cf. REB, NET Bible

"They" refers to the people of Israel.

▣ "Everyone receives of Your words" This refers to the giving of the law at Mt. Sinai/Horeb in Exodus 19-20 and
following. God's people knew God's will and law. The covenant people have a special responsibility to reflect God's character.

All of them affirmed their willingness to follow God's law.

verses.zh: 摩西将律法传给我们，作为雅各会众的产业。
verses.en: Moses delivered to us a law,[NOTE:1] an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
notes: The Hebrew term תּוֹרָה (torah) here should be understood more broadly as instruction.
verses.commentary:
33:4 "Moses charged us with a law" This seems to confirm the idea in the preceding verses that the reference in
Deut. 33:3 is to a place name and that these verses are talking about God's people, not angels.

▣ "A possession for the assembly of Jacob" The term "possession" (BDB 440) refers to an inheritance
(BDB 439). It was used first of the tribe of Israel (Jacob, BDB 784) in Exod. 6:8 and is mentioned often in Ezekiel
(cf. Ezek. 11:15; 33:24; 36:2,3,5).

The term "assembly" (BDB 875) means "congregation" (cf. same root in Deut. 23:2,3,4,8; 31:30).

Because of the parallelism in Deut. 33:4, this particular usage of "possession" may be imagery for
the covenant (i.e. law). God's people possess a revelation as well as a land!

verses.zh: 百姓的众首领，以色列的各支派，一同聚会的时候，耶和华（原文是他）在耶书仑中为王。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] was king over Jeshurun,[NOTE:2] when the leaders of the people assembled,the tribes of Israel together.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he was king.” The present translation avoids the sudden shift in person and the mistaken impression that Moses is the referent by specifying the referent as “the Lord.”
Jeshurun is a term of affection referring to Israel, derived from the Hebrew verb יָשַׁר (yashar, “be upright”). See note on the term in Deut 32:15.
The following blessing is given to the tribes in order, although the tribe of Simeon is curiously missing from the list.
verses.commentary:
33:5 "He was king" This is a reference to YHWH as King (BDB 572 I, cf. Exod. 15:18; Num. 23:21; 24:7;
1 Sam. 8:4-9; Ps. 29:10).

▣ The last two lines parallel "heads of the people" and "the tribes of Israel." It refers to the inauguration
of the covenant with the new people of God at Mt. Sinai/Horeb (cf. Exodus 19-20).

▣ "Jeshurun" This is literally "the upright ones" (BDB 449) and refers to Israel (cf. Deut. 33:26; 32:15; Isa. 44:2).

verses.zh: 愿流便存活，不致死亡；愿他人数不致稀少。
verses.en: “May Reuben live and not die,and may his people multiply.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and [not] may his men be few” (cf. KJV, NASB, NIV).
verses.commentary:
33:6 "May Reuben live and not die" Verse 6 has three Qal JUSSIVE forms:

- live ‒ BDB 310, KB 309

- die ‒ BDB 559, KB 562 (negated)

- be ‒ BDB 224, KB 243 (negated)

Reuben was the firstborn of Jacob, but he sinned against his father (cf. Gen. 35:22) and lost his preeminence (cf. Gen. 49:3-4).

▣

NASB
"Nor his men be few"

NKJV
"nor let his men be free"

NRSV
"even though his numbers are few"

TEV
"although their people are few"

NJB
"though his men be few"

REB
"may he be few in number"

JPSOA
"though few be his number"

Peshitta
"Let his people be numerous"

LXX
"Let him be many in number"

This is part of the loss of preeminence (cf. TEV, NJB). This phrase often means "not very many men"
(cf. Gen. 34:30; Deut. 4:27; Ps. 105:12; Jer. 44:28).

verses.zh: 为犹大祝福说：求耶和华俯听犹大的声音，引导他归于本族；他曾用手为自己争战，你必帮助他攻击敌人。
verses.en: And this is the blessing[NOTE:1] to Judah. He said,“Listen, O Lord, to Judah’s voice,and bring him to his people.May his power be great,and may you help him against his foes.”
notes: The words “the blessing” are supplied in the translation for clarity and stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
33:7 "Hear" This VERB (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used
often in Deuteronomy, but usually it is YHWH (or Moses) speaking to Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (Shema)

▣ "O Lord" See SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "the voice of Judah" In context Moses is asking YHWH to hear Judah's prayer (i.e. the tribe of Judah's
prayer). There is nothing in Moses' blessing that hints of Judah's special place as royal tribe, so evident in Jacob's
blessing of Gen. 49:8-12.

The fact that the tribe of Simeon is not mentioned in chapter 33 has caused some to relate this prophecy to a later
period when Simeon was incorporated into Judah (cf. Josh. 19:1-9; Jdgs. 1:3-4). Simeon's allotment was southwest of Judah, which
was adjacent to the five powerful Philistine city-states.

▣

NASB
"With his hands he contended for them"

NKJV
"Let his hands be sufficient for him"

NRSV, REB
"strengthen his hands for him"

TEV
"Fight for them, Lord"

NJB
"that his hands may defend his rights"

Peshitta
"Let his hands contend for him"

LXX
"his hand will decide for him"

This Hebrew phrase is uncertain. It may refer to Judah defending itself against enemies, which may
point toward the division of the unified monarchy in 922 B.C. into Judah and Israel (only speculation).

verses.zh: 论利未说：耶和华啊，你的土明和乌陵都在你的虔诚人那里。你在玛撒曾试验他，在米利巴水与他争论。
verses.en: Of Levi he said:“Your Thummim and Urim[NOTE:1] belong to your godly one,[NOTE:2] whose authority you challenged at Massah,[NOTE:3] and with whom you argued at the waters of Meribah.[NOTE:4]
notes: Thummim and Urim. These terms, whose meaning is uncertain, refer to sacred stones carried in a pouch on the breastplate of the high priest and examined on occasion as a means of ascertaining God’s will or direction. See Exod 28:30; Lev 8:8; Num 27:21; 1 Sam 28:6. See also C. Van Dam, NIDOTTE 1:329-31.
Heb “godly man.” The reference is probably to Moses as representative of the whole tribe of Levi.
Massah means “testing” in Hebrew; the name is a wordplay on what took place there. Cf. Exod 17:7; Deut 6:16; 9:22; Ps 95:8-9.
Meribah means “contention, argument” in Hebrew; this is another wordplay on the incident that took place there. Cf. Num 20:13, 24; Ps 106:32.
verses.commentary:
33:8-11 In the Qumran literature, scrolls found in caves northwest of the Dead Sea, Deut. 18:18 and Num. 24:15-17,
have definite Messianic prophecies linked with this passage. They thought that the Messiah was related to the
tribe of Levi (cf. Ps. 110:4-7; Zechariah 3-4).

This blessing includes not only the past faithful acts of Aaron (cf. Ps. 106:16), but also of Moses
(cf. last two lines of Deut. 33:8 and Exod. 17:1-7).

33:8 "Your Thummim and Your Urim" These two items (BDB 1070 and BDB 22) were

- a mechanical way (i.e. lots)

- a visible light which denoted a prophecy to know the will of YHWH

- Apparently they were kept by the High Priest in a pouch behind the breast plate (cf. Exod. 28:30; Lev. 8:8; 1 Sam. 14:37-42; 23:9-12).

- Exactly what they were and how they worked has been lost (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 329-331).

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

▣ "Your godly man" This may refer to Aaron or Moses or the descendant of the High Priest, but the historical
reference mentioned refers to Moses.

▣ "Massah. . .Meribah" Read Exod. 17:7. However, the rebellion at this location did not mention Levi or the
priests in any way. The exact connection is uncertain.

▣ Apparently YHWH tested both Israel and her leadership during the wilderness wandering period to see if
they really trusted Him and His care and guidance (cf. Exod. 17:7).

- proved/tested ‒ BDB 650, KB 702, Piel PERFECT

- strive/contend ‒ BDB 936, KB 1224, Qal IMPERFECT

Notice that YHWH regularly tests (BDB 650) the motives and commitment of those who claim to know and trust Him:

- Abraham ‒ Genesis 22

- Israel ‒ Exod. 15:25; 16:4; 20:20; Deut. 8:2,16; 13:3 Jdg. 2:22; 3:1,4

- Moses ‒ Deut. 33:8

- Hezekiah ‒ 2 Chr. 32:31

- Jesus was also tested ‒ Matthew 4; Luke 4

This same word is used often for humans "testing" God, which is always seen in a negative light!

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TEXTS HIS PEOPLE

verses.zh: 他论自己的父母说：我未曾看见；他也不承认弟兄，也不认识自己的儿女。这是因利未人遵行你的话，谨守你的约。
verses.en: He said to his father and mother, ‘I have not seen him,’[NOTE:1] and he did not acknowledge his own brothersor know his own children,for they kept your word,and guarded your covenant.
notes: This statement no doubt alludes to the Levites’ destruction of their own fellow tribesmen following the golden calf incident (Exod 32:25-29).
verses.commentary:
33:9 This refers to the passage in Exodus 32, where Israel became involved in idolatry in the making and
worshiping (i.e. sexual orgy) of the golden calf. At this point Moses ordered the faithful Levites (his own tribe) to kill
many of their fellow Israelites in judgment (cf. Deut. 32:25-29).

By this action, even against their own family, they are honored for:

- they observed Your word ‒ BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 29:9

- they kept Your covenant ‒ BDB 665, KB 718, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 25:10; 78:7;
119:2,22, 33,34,56,69,100,115,129,145

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 他们要将你的典章教训雅各，将你的律法教训以色列。他们要把香焚在你面前，把全牲的燔祭献在你的坛上。
verses.en: They will teach Jacob your ordinancesand Israel your law;they will offer incense as a pleasant odor, and a whole offering on your altar.
verses.commentary:
33:10 "teach. . .put incense. . .and whole burnt offerings" These are the duties of the Levitical priests:

- teaching ‒ BDB 434, KB 436, Hiphil IMPERFECT, cf. Deut. 31:9-13, which
includes judging, cf. Deut. 17:9-10

- duties at the tabernacle/temple

- remember, in Deuteronomy there is no disctinction bewteen the duties of the priests and Levites (i.e. Deut. 18:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

▣ "to Jacob. . .to Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

verses.zh: 求耶和华降福在他的财物上，悦纳他手里所办的事。那些起来攻击他和恨恶他的人，愿你刺透他们的腰，使他们不得再起来。
verses.en: Bless, O Lord, his goods,and be pleased with his efforts;undercut the legs[NOTE:1] of any who attack him,and of those who hate him, so that they cannot stand.”
notes: Heb “smash the sinews [or “loins,” so many English versions].” This part of the body was considered to be center of one’s strength (cf. Job 40:16; Ps 69:24; Prov 31:17; Nah 2:2, 11). See J. H. Tigay, Deuteronomy (JPSTC), 325.
verses.commentary:
33:11 This short verse has four VERBS and two PARTICIPLES:

- "bless" ‒ BDB 138, KB 159, Piel IMPERATIVE, cf. Deut. 33:1,13,20,24; 28:3 (twice),4,5,6 (twice),8,12,19;
30:16. This is what YHWH wants to do!

- "accept" ‒ BDB 953, KB 1280, Qal IMPERFECT. This is a sacrificial term, cf. Lev. 1:4;
7:18; 19:7; 22:23,25,27, which can also mean "enjoy," Lev. 26:34 (twice)

- "shatter" ‒ BDB 563, KB 571, Qal IMPERATIVE, used of YHWH in Deut. 32:39, here
of their enemies (cf. #4, #5, and #6)

- "those who rise up" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, used of adversaries

- to God, Exod. 15:7

- to Israel, Exod. 32:25; Ps. 109:28

- to one's neighbor, Deut. 19:11

- "those who hate him" ‒ BDB 971, KB 1338, Piel PARTICIPLE, often in the Psalms
for enemies, cf. Deut. 18:40; 44:7,10; 55:12; 68:1; 89:23

- "rise again" (negated) ‒ same root as #4, but here a Qal IMPERFECT. This could
refer to the other Israelites who attacked Moses' and Aaron's leadership during the wilderness wandering period.

▣

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"bless his substance"

TEV
"help their tribe to grow

strong"

NJB
"bless his worthiness"

REB
"bless his powers"

LXX
"bless his strength"

This term (BDB 298) can have several connotations:

- its basic meaning is "capacity" or "power"

- "strength"

- "ability," "skills"

- "worthiness"

- "accomplishments"

- "possessions"

▣ "Shatter the loins" This is literally "break the thigh" (i.e. the largest muscle in the body used as a
symbol for the whole person). This is Hebrew imagery for making someone powerless. It is even possible that it
has the connotation of stopping procreation, thereby, no future generations.

verses.zh: 论便雅悯说：耶和华所亲爱的必同耶和华安然居住；耶和华终日遮蔽他，也住在他两肩之中。
verses.en: Of Benjamin he said:“The beloved of the Lord will live safely by him;he protects him all the time, and the Lord[NOTE:1] places him on his chest.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “between his shoulders.” This suggests the scene in John 13:23 with Jesus and the Beloved Disciple.
verses.commentary:
33:12 "Of Benjamin. . .beloved of the Lord" He (BDB 122) may be called "beloved
of the Lord" because he was the favorite of his father, Jacob (cf. Gen. 44:20).

▣ "dwell in security by Him" The VERB (BDB 1014, KB 1496, is a Qal
IMPERFECT, but in a JUSSSIVE sense, cf. Deut. 33:12 [twice],16,20,28;
Exod. 25:8; 29:45,46; JPSOA does not translate this as a JUSSSIVE, but as a statement). YHWH is
their close companion in Deut. 33:12.

The MT has "by Him" in line 2 but this word may be an ancient name for Deity. The UBS Text Project,
p. 312, suggests "most-high." The LXX translates it as "God overshadows him all the days," which, if correct, shows this
Divine name must start line 3 (NRSV, NJB, REB).

This ancient name (עלו, BDB 752-754, usually a PREPOSITION)
for Deity might also appear in 1 Sam. 2:10, line 2.

▣

NASB, REB
"Who shields him all the day"

NKJV
"who shelters him all the day long"

NRSV
"surrounds him all day long"

TEV
"He guards them all the day long"

NJB
"protects him day after day"

JPSOA
"ever does protect him"

Peshitta
"The Lord shall have compassion on him"

LXX
"God over shadows him all day long"

The VERB (BDB 342, KB 339, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) is used
only here and can mean "to enclose" or "to surround" or "to cover."

▣

NASB, NKJV
"dwells between His shoulders"

NRSV, LXX, JPSOA
"rest between his shoulders"

TEV
"he dwells in their midst"

NJB
"dwells between his hillsides"

This is imagery for

- a place of peace and security (Deut. 33:20,28)

- living in a sheltered place (i.e. Shiloh, Bethel, or Jerusalem [a suggestion of S. R. Driver])

verses.zh: 论约瑟说：愿他的地蒙耶和华赐福，得天上的宝物、甘露，以及地里所藏的泉水；
verses.en: Of Joseph he said:“May the Lord bless his landwith the harvest produced by the sky,[NOTE:1] by the dew,and by the depths crouching beneath;
notes: Heb “from the harvest of the heavens.” The referent appears to be good crops produced by the rain that falls from the sky.
verses.commentary:
33:13-17 The longest of the blessings, except for Levi, goes to the sons of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh
(cf. Deut. 33:17, Joseph's two sonsby Egyptian wives). These were the most powerful of the northern tribes.

- In Deut. 33:13-16b Moses enumerates agricultural blessings on these two tribes.

- In Deut. 33:16c,d Joseph's status in Egypt is acknowledged.

- In Deut. 33:17 the power of these two tribes is expressed in animal imagery.

33:13 This verse refers to the abundance of moisture from dew and underground sources (cf. Gen. 49:25). Water
meant agricultural abundance (cf. Gen. 49:25)!

verses.zh: 得太阳所晒熟的美果，月亮所养成的宝物；
verses.en: with the harvest produced by the daylight[NOTE:1] and by[NOTE:2] the moonlight;[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “goings forth of the sun.”
Heb “and from the harvest of the yield of.” This has been simplified in the translation to avoid redundancy.
Heb “the moon.” Many English versions regard this as a reference to “months” (“moons”) rather than the moon itself (cf. NAB, NASB, NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 得上古之山的至宝，永世之岭的宝物；
verses.en: with the best[NOTE:1] of the ancient mountainsand the harvest produced by the age-old hills;
notes: Heb “head” or “top.”
verses.commentary:
33:15 "the best things of the ancient mountains. . .And. . .of the everlasting hills" This may refer to trees, both for
food and construction.

verses.zh: 得地和其中所充满的宝物，并住荆棘中上主的喜悦。愿这些福都归于约瑟的头上，归于那与弟兄迥别之人的顶上。
verses.en: with the harvest of the earth and its fullnessand the pleasure of him who resided in the burning bush.[NOTE:1] May blessing rest on Joseph’s head,and on the top of the head of the one set apart[NOTE:2] from his brothers.
notes: The expression “him who resided in the bush” is frequently understood as a reference to the appearance of the Lord to Moses at Sinai from a burning bush (so NIV, NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT; cf. Exod 2:2-6; 3:2, 4). To make this reference clear the word “burning” is supplied in the translation.
This apparently refers to Joseph’s special status among his brothers as a result of his being chosen by God to save the family from the famine and to lead Egypt.
verses.commentary:
33:16 "And the favor of Him who dwelt in the bush" This may refer to the burning bush (cf. Exod. 3:2-4). This word
for bush (BDB 702) is used only five times in the OT, four of them in Exod. 3:2-4.

verses.en: May the firstborn of his bull bring him honor,and may his horns be those of a wild ox;with them may he gore all peoples,all the far reaches of the earth.They are the ten thousands of Ephraim,[NOTE:1] and they are the thousands of Manasseh.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Ephraim and Manasseh were the sons of Joseph who became founders of the two tribes into which Joseph’s descendants were split (Gen 48:19-20). Jacob’s blessing granted favored status to Ephraim; this is probably why Ephraim is viewed here as more numerous than Manasseh.
Or “acceptable”; Heb “righteous” (so NASB).

33:17 "And his horns are the horns of the wild ox" In Hebrew the word "horn" (BDB 901) is a symbol of power.

verses.zh: 论西布伦说：西布伦哪，你出外可以欢喜。以萨迦啊，在你帐棚里可以快乐。
verses.en: Of Zebulun he said:“Rejoice, Zebulun, when you go outside, and Issachar, when you are in your tents.
verses.commentary:
33:18 "Of Zebulun. . .And, Issachar" These two tribes are also listed together as in Gen. 49:13-15.

▣ "Rejoice" This VERB (BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERATIVE) is used
in the sense of "enjoy the good, safe abundance of life."

▣ "going forth" This (BDB 422, KB 425, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) seems to be used
in the sense of a free life (cf. Deut. 28:6,19; 31:2).

▣ "in your tents" This (BDB 13) refers to their home during the wilderness wandering period, but
became imagery for one's house.

These two parallel lines imply a happy, settled life.

verses.zh: 他们要将列邦召到山上，在那里献公义的祭；因为他们要吸取海里的丰富，并沙中所藏的珍宝。
verses.en: They will summon peoples to the mountain,there they will sacrifice proper[NOTE:1] sacrifices;for they will enjoy[NOTE:2] the abundance of the seas,and the hidden treasures of the shores.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “suck.”
Heb “of the sand” (so NRSV, NLT); CEV “the sandy beach.”
Heb “forehead,” picturing Gad attacking prey.
verses.commentary:
33:19 The parallelism between "mountain" (BDB 249) and "offer righteous sacrifices" (cf. Ps. 4:5; 51:19) implies
a worship setting (cf. Exod. 15:17).

The next interpretive question is, "Do the next two lines of poetry continue this thought or change
to another topic?" Zebulun's involvement in the sea is mentioned in Gen. 49:13.

▣ "abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand" These two lines are parallel. They are
both OBJECTS of one VERB, "suck" or "draw out" (BDB 413, KB 416, Qal IMPERFECT).
This is imagery for abundance (cf. Deut. 32:13).

- The first one refers to:

- food (i.e. sacrifices or good living)

- merchandise (i.e. coral, shells, sponges or dye)

- The second is made up of two Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLES:

- "to cover," but only here it means "reserved" or "laid up" (BDB 706)

- "to hide" (BDB 380)

They seem to refer to the shipping trade (cf. Gen. 49:13-14).

verses.zh: 论迦得说：使迦得扩张的应当称颂！迦得住如母狮；他撕裂膀臂，连头顶也撕裂。
verses.en: Of Gad he said:“Blessed be the one who enlarges Gad.Like a lioness he will dwell;he will tear at an arm—indeed, a scalp.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew term מְחֹקֵק (mekhoqeq; Poel participle of חָקַק, khaqaq, “to inscribe”) reflects the idea that the recorder of allotments (the “ruler”) is able to set aside for himself the largest and best. See E. H. Merrill, Deuteronomy (NAC), 444-45.
verses.commentary:
33:20 "Blessed is the one who enlarges Gad" This seems to be a reference to YHWH.

▣ "He lies down as a lion" The word is "lioness" (BDB 522, cf. Gen. 49:9; Num. 24:9; Job 4:11). The
lioness was the one who hunted and provided food for the male lion and cubs. Gad was referred to as the lioness. The
tribe of Gad was blessed because of their faithfulness in battle (cf. Gen. 49:19).

verses.zh: 他为自己选择头一段地，因在那里有设立律法者的分存留。他与百姓的首领同来；他施行耶和华的公义和耶和华与以色列所立的典章。
verses.en: He has selected the best part for himself,for the portion of the ruler[NOTE:1] is set aside[NOTE:2] there;he came with the leaders[NOTE:3] of the people,he obeyed the righteous laws of the Lordand his ordinances with Israel.”
notes: Heb “covered in” (if from the root סָפַן, safan; cf. HALOT 764-65 s.v. ספן qal).
Heb “heads” (in the sense of chieftains).
He will leap forth from Bashan. This may refer to Dan’s conquest of Laish, a region just to the west of Bashan (Judg 18:27-28).
verses.commentary:
33:21 This verse is a play on Gad or a valiant warrior (in the imagery of a lion). He chose part of the land
on the eastern side of Jordan to inherit, but he and the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh were the first
military group to go into battle in the Promised Land (cf. Josh. 4:12-13; 22:1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIONS (OT)

▣ "For there the ruler's portion was reserved" The Hebrew meaning is uncertain! JPSOA translates the
line of poetry as "For there is the portion of the revered chieftain."

▣ "And he came with the leaders of the people" This may refer to

- these three tribes asking Moses and the elders for permission to settle on the eastern side of Jordan

- these three tribes going into battle first on the western side of the Lordan (cf. Josh. 4:12)

verses.zh: 论但说：但为小狮子，从巴珊跳出来。
verses.en: Of Dan he said:“Dan is a lion’s cub;he will leap forth from Bashan.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Dip his foot in olive oil. This is a metaphor for prosperity, one especially apt in light of the abundance of olive groves in the area settled by Asher. The Hebrew term refers to olive oil, which symbolizes blessing in the OT. See R. Way, NIDOTTE 4:171-73.
verses.commentary:
33:22 "Dan is a lion's whelp, that leaps from Bashan" The mention of Dan as somehow connected to Bashan
(cf. Deut. 1:4; 3:1,3,4,10,11,13,14) is surprising. Originally Dan's tribal allocation by lot was in the southwest
(i.e. the Philistine area) and later they moved to the far north (cf. Judges 18). This may be a prophecy connected to
this unauthorized relocation.

verses.zh: 论拿弗他利说：拿弗他利啊，你足沾恩惠，满得耶和华的福，可以得西方和南方为业。
verses.en: Of Naphtali he said:“O Naphtali, overflowing with favor,and full of the Lord’s blessing,possess the west and south.”
verses.commentary:
33:23 "Take possession of the sea and the south" The VERB (BDB 439, KB 441, Qal
IMPERATIVE) is used several times in Deuteronomy for Israel to possess the land (cf. Deut. 1:8,21,39;
2:24,31; 9:23; 11:31; 17:14; 26:1). It implies a taking by force and securing it as a permanent inheritance.

verses.zh: 论亚设说：愿亚设享受多子的福乐，得他弟兄的喜悦，可以把脚蘸在油中。
verses.en: Of Asher he said:“Asher is blessed with children;may he be favored by his brothers,and may he dip his foot in olive oil.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “of your gates” have been supplied in the translation to clarify the referent of “bars.”
verses.commentary:
33:24 "Of Asher he said

'More blessed than sons is Asher;

May he be favored by his brothers'" This VERB (BDB 224, KB 243, "be") is a
Qal JUSSIVE. This shows the working of the Hebrew mind. To an Israelite, a son was the greatest
blessing possible.

The rabbis interpret this verse to mean that because of the extreme beauty of Asher's daughters they
were more sought after than sons. The meaning of the MT text is uncertain.

▣ "And may he dip his foot in oil" The location of Asher, on the northern seacoast, is the best area for
growing olive trees. This phrase possibly refers to the act of treading oil out of the olives by foot.

verses.zh: 你的门闩（或译：鞋）是铜的，铁的。你的日子如何，你的力量也必如何。
verses.en: The bars of your gates[NOTE:1] will be made of iron and bronze,and may you have lifelong strength.”
notes: Jeshurun is a term of affection referring to Israel, derived from the Hebrew verb יָשַׁר (yashar, “be upright”). See note on the term in Deut 32:15.
verses.commentary:
33:25 "Your locks will be iron and bronze" The Hebrew root for "locks" (BDB 653) or "bars" (BDB 653) can
also be translated "shoes" (BDB 653). The form used here is found only here. Because of Asher's geographical position,
on the major highway route from the Fertile Crescent down to Egypt, if Asher fell, the whole land fell (from a northerly
invasion). She was considered "the door and lock" to the Promised Land.

verses.zh: 耶书仑哪，没有能比　神的。他为帮助你，乘在天空，显其威荣，驾行穹苍。
verses.en: “There is no one like God, O Jeshurun,[NOTE:1] who rides through the sky[NOTE:2] to help you, on the clouds in majesty.
notes: Or “(who) rides (on) the heavens” (cf. NIV, NRSV, NLT). This title depicts Israel’s God as sovereign over the elements of the storm (cf. Ps 68:33). The use of the phrase here may be polemical; Moses may be asserting that Israel’s God, not Baal (called the “rider of the clouds” in the Ugaritic myths), is the true divine king (cf. v. 5) who controls the elements of the storm, grants agricultural prosperity, and delivers his people from their enemies. See R. B. Chisholm, Jr., “The Polemic against Baalism in Israel’s Early History and Literature,” BSac 151 (1994): 275.

Heb “and from under, arms of perpetuity.” The words “you” and “his” are supplied in the translation for clarification. Some have perceived this line to be problematic and have offered alternative translations that differ significantly from the present translation: “He spread out the primeval tent; he extended the ancient canopy” (NAB); “He subdues the ancient gods, shatters the forces of old” (NRSV). These are based on alternate meanings or conjectural emendations rather than textual variants in the mss and versions.
verses.commentary:
33:26-29 These verses are a transition section which praises YHWH's uniqueness and power! Jeshurun is
used as a designation for Israel (cf. Deut. 32:15). These verses (i.e. Deut. 33:26 line b & c; Deut. 33:28 line c &d;
Deut. 33:29 line f) use phrases that commonly referred to the fertility god, Ba'al, implying that all the things that
had been said about Ba'al were not true about him, but were true of YHWH. YHWH is the only God.

33:26 "There is none like the God" Sees note at Deut. 4:35.

This term "dwelling place" (BDB 733) can refer to an animal's lair (cf. Job 37:8; 38:40; Amos 3:4) or imagery

This is such a famous and encouraging verse. However, the MT is uncertain (i.e. JPSOA footnote).
Here are the options.

- NRSV ‒ "He subdues the ancient gods"

- REB ‒ "He subdued te ancient powers"

- Peshitta ‒ "In the heaven of heavens is the dwelling of our God"

- LXX ‒ "And there is divine protection of yore"

Verses 26-27 continue the imagery of YHWH as Israel's (i.e. Jeshsurun) divine warrior (cf. vv. 2-5).

▣ "And underneath are the everlasting arms" This is imagery for:

- YHWH's fighting on their behalf (cf. line c, Deut. 33:29)

- YHWH's perpetual care and attention

YHWH is the God who acts! It is possible that this is an allusion to Gen. 49:24 (lines b & c).

▣ "Destroy" This VERB (BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil IMPERATIVE)
means "to exterminate." It is part of the terminology of "holy war," cf. Deut. 1:27; 2:22; 6:15; 9:20; Josh. 7:12; 9:24. If Israel
is obedient to the covenant He will fight for them, but if not, He will fight against them (i.e. the Mosaic covenant is conditional)!

The Israelites were expected to dress for battle and take the field against her enemies, but it was
YHWH who won the battle! Notice how YHWH's sovereignty and human actions work together.

K. A. Kitchen, Ancient Orient and Old Testament, pp. 164-165, has an interesting note about the
word "Bãmã" (BDB 119).

"A lost meaning is sometimes recovered for a well-known word. 'Bãmã' is the common
Hebrew word for a high place. In Ugaritic, it also means 'back,' and this rendering would also fit very well in Deuteronomy 33:29,
in the ancient Blessing of Moses:

Thine enemies shall submit to thee,

And thou shalt tread upon their backs'

(rather than: 'on their high places').

The idea expressed is then similar to that in Joshua 10:24 or in Psalm 110:1, and finds plastic
expression in Egyptian reliefs and statuary."

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter is very similar to Genesis 49. Both reflect the ancient Jewish tradition of a Patriarchal blessing
on the children (i.e. Jacob to his sons in Genesis 49). Here Moses is a surrogate father to the tribes of Israel
and pronounces the family blessing and warning on each one.

- The song of chapter 32, with its severe warnings, must be combined with the blessing of Deuteronomy 33 to
see the full counsel of YHWH's word (i.e. curses and blessings, cf. Lev. 26; Deut. 28).!

- This poem seems to break the continuity between Deut. 32:48-52 and Deut. 34. Why it was inserted here, when
and by whom, cannot be answered. It is assumed to be an inspired poetic blessing linked to Moses.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 33:1-5

1 Now this is the blessing with which Moses the man of God blessed the sons of Israel before his death.

2He said, "The Lord came from Sinai,

And dawned on them from Seir;

He shone forth from Mount Paran,

And He came from the midst of ten thousand holy ones;

At His right hand there was flashing lightning for them.

3Indeed, He loves the people;

All Your holy ones are in Your hand,

And they followed in Your steps;

Everyone receives of Your words.

4Moses charged us with a law,

A possession for the assembly of Jacob.

5And He was king in Jeshurun,

When the heads of the people were gathered,

The tribes of Israel together."
